Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is 5-azacytidine, a highly polar ribonucleoside (logD -3.17, TPSA 143.7); L4 Caco-2 records for levovirin (0.12×10^-6 cm/s) and gemcitabine (<1×10^-6 and 0.99×10^-6 cm/s) show low passive permeability for polar ribonucleoside/cytidine analogs.

L5 Caco-2/MDCK records extend this pattern: EFdA A→B Papp ~4-6×10^-7 cm/s (C60, C64) and GS-441524 A→B Papp 0.229×10^-6 cm/s with BCRP/MDR1 efflux (C62, C65, C67, C70) indicate low permeability plus efflux for other nucleoside analogs.

L5 efflux experiments show cladribine is a BCRP substrate (efflux ratio reduced to 1.09 with Ko143; C59/C68/C69), supporting gut-wall efflux as a plausible presystemic loss mechanism for polar nucleosides.

L5 transporter-uptake records for gemcitabine (C61) and NHC (C66) show some cytidine-like nucleosides are substrates of intestinal nucleoside transporters; this could partially mitigate low passive permeability, but no F outcome is attached and it does not affirmatively establish F>=20.

Direct high-F records for emtricitabine (92%, C16/C33) and didanosine (30-54%, C13/C32) are gold outcomes for other nucleoside scaffolds (oxathiolane/dideoxy) and are less transferable to the ribonucleoside query; acyclovir's 20% (C06) is at the threshold and does not affirmatively support F>=20.

L3 lamivudine exposure records (C40, C44) demonstrate rapid absorption and measurable AUC after oral dosing, but they are exposure endpoints without F and use an oxathiolane nucleoside scaffold, so they do not provide affirmative F>=20 evidence for the ribonucleoside query.
